findings.text: follow-on: the --stage error branch still emits "persisted": not dry_run (a bool) and no "failed", but _print_summary now sums r.get("persisted",0) and renders it per IDS, so an error-only run prints "<ids>: True bindings persisted" and drops the binding count it previously reported via bindings; this path is untested (the summary test drives map_run through a patched _run_plain_mode).

follow-on: _claimed_source_id compares _source_group_key, which drops everything up to the first colon, so a model entry naming a different facility's same-named source (e.g. tcv:X for a batch claimed by jt-60sa:X) is accepted as the claimed source rather than refused; the "a model entry naming another source is refused" guarantee holds only within the facility prefix, which the design treats as free text the model may mistype.

justifications.fit: The change reuses the existing escalation machinery (EscalationFlag / EscalationSeverity.ERROR) and the existing CandidateWriteError from graph_ops rather than inventing a second failure channel; write_mapping_bindings sits beside its single owner write_mapping_binding in models.py; the exit-on-failure is a plain SystemExit(1) from the click command. No plan, sprint or ticket identifier appears in any symbol, comment, docstring or the test module name; the test module is named for the behaviour (test_binding_source_identity).
justifications.goal_fidelity: §22's three fixes are all present. (1) validate_mappings at mapping.py:1665-1700 takes each batch's claimed source from sections.assignments and rewrites every binding through _claimed_source_id (mapping.py:1638-1649), so a mistyped facility prefix persists against the real SignalSource; a model entry whose source group key differs is refused as an EscalationFlag naming both ids (mapping.py:1677-1691). (2) write_mapping_bindings (models.py:594-628) records a graph-refused binding with its reason while persist_mapping_result (models.py:798-802) continues to its siblings, and validate_worker threads state.binding_failures through (workers.py:1193-1203) so the next IDS persists. (3) _print_summary (map.py:658-691) counts persisted bindings and map_run raises SystemExit(1) on any failure (map.py:371-372). Each binding is still programmatically validated, so the fix names the source without skipping validation.
justifications.reuse: write_mapping_bindings calls the single owner write_mapping_binding (graph_ops.py:695-760) per binding and does not spell the Cypher a second time; persist_mapping_result routes its binding loop through it once (models.py:798) rather than duplicating; _claimed_source_id reuses _source_group_key, the same key the error-signal matcher uses (mapping.py:1937), so prefix normalisation has one definition. The workers state fields bindings_persisted / bindings_failed extend the existing bindings_total / bindings_passed counters rather than adding a parallel shape.
justifications.scope_discipline: The commit's six changed paths (imas_codex/ids/mapping.py, imas_codex/ids/models.py, imas_codex/ids/workers.py, imas_codex/cli/map.py, tests/ids/test_binding_source_identity.py, docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-mapping-study-expansion/binding-source-from-claim.html) are exactly the run's six declared write paths, and git show --stat lists no seventh path.
